description: INT-368 (files/10 §8; KVKK 2018/10 measure 3ç): Renovate follows updates for every lockfile and pin in this repository - uv, pnpm, container digests and GitHub Actions.
Security updates open at once, outside the weekly schedule. Nothing is ever merged automatically: every update is a pull request that runs the CI, security and licence gates and waits for a human.
No preset is extended, so every behaviour is stated here. tests/ci/test_dependency_updates.py pins it; docs/runbooks/dependency-updates.md is the maintainer's procedure.
prFooter: Renovate never merges this. To merge it, carry it under a backlog issue - an `INT-xxx:` title, `Closes #n`, the issue's `Sec-Row` and docs/evidence/INT-xxx.md - as docs/runbooks/dependency-updates.md describes; the evidence and sec_row gates refuse it until then.

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

customManagers.description: The two digest-pinned image references that live outside a Dockerfile or compose file: the staging object-store image (infra/staging/lib.sh) and its single source of truth in the model registry (observability/registry.yaml, INT-347). tests/infra/test_object_store_image.py requires every copy to agree, so all of them move in the container-images group.

The isolation probe's image for the intake-aws-ci runner pool (infra/ci/aws-runner/runner.conf PROBE_IMAGE, INT-467): every runner publishes a port from it at once, and it is pulled by digest into each runner's rootless daemon.

packageRules.description: Container images and GitHub Actions are pinned by digest (CLAUDE.md invariant 14); the tag stays beside the digest as its readable label.
Constraints are not versions: the interpreter floor, engines, the package manager field and the security overrides keep their range and move only when a release falls outside it.
A peer dependency range is widened, never pinned.
Python (uv.lock and the hash-pinned staging requirements): one weekly PR for minor and patch updates.
Node (pnpm-lock.yaml): one weekly PR for minor and patch updates.
Container images (Dockerfiles, compose files and the regex-managed references): one weekly PR for minor, patch and digest updates.
GitHub Actions (SHA pins with the tag in a trailing comment): one weekly PR for minor, patch and digest updates.
pre-commit hook revisions: one weekly PR for minor, patch and digest updates.

The Keycloak provider's Maven build (infra/keycloak/providers/webauthn-session-notes: pom.xml and the wrapper's Maven distribution): one weekly PR for minor and patch updates. The same PR re-records the module's .mvn/checksums and the jar pin, or the check-py CI job's provider build refuses it (docs/runbooks/keycloak-realm.md §3).

The provider compiles against the Keycloak it runs in, so the Keycloak image and the org.keycloak artefacts move in one PR (tests/admin/test_webauthn_session_notes_provider.py holds keycloak.version to the compose tag).

The Expo SDK moves as a unit (`npx expo install --fix` picks the compatible set), so its packages share one PR that waits for a maintainer to ask for it on the Dependency Dashboard. A security fix is not held back: vulnerabilityAlerts overrides this.

The ruff pre-commit rev tracks the ruff pin in the dev dependencies; a mismatch makes the hook and make check-py fight over formatting (.pre-commit-config.yaml). Both halves carry the same cooldown, so neither enters the group PR without the other.

The object-store image is tagged RELEASE.<date>T<time>Z; this versioning lets Renovate order those tags instead of only refreshing the digest. Docker Hub carries the release timestamp the cooldown needs.

Supply-chain cooldown: a regular npm or PyPI release is proposed only after it has been public for seven days, long enough for a compromised release to be caught and yanked (semgrep p/ci renovate-missing-minimum-release-age). Every rule that names packages or dependency types carries the same cooldown. Security updates skip it: vulnerabilityAlerts clears minimumReleaseAge.
The same seven-day cooldown for Maven Central releases (the Keycloak provider's build and test dependencies and its plugins).
A major update is its own PR and waits for a maintainer to ask for it on the Dependency Dashboard; a major that fixes a vulnerability does not wait.
A new Python minor (the interpreter in the base image or in .python-version) is a platform decision, not a routine update.
The interpreter line in .python-version moves only on request.
